History:
- Presenting complaint: New swelling of the left elbow noticed about 1 week ago. Swelling is somewhat warm but not painful; patient can move the elbow normally. No clear injury or trauma reported; observed in the shower.
- Onset/duration/progression: Swelling appeared about one week ago; no prior similar episodes.
- Context: Desk-based work; engages in running 2–3 times per week.
- Associated symptoms: None reported.
- Past Medical History: Osteoarthritis diagnosed by GP a few years ago.
- Allergies: Peanut allergy.
- Medications: No regular medications.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis (diagnosed by GP, several years ago).
- Allergies: Peanut.
- Medications: None currently.

Physical Examination:
- Left elbow with swelling.
- Skin over swelling slightly warm and dry.
- Patient able to move elbow normally; no focal tenderness reported.
- No signs of septic arthritis observed during exam.
- No other acute findings documented.

Impression:
- Suspected left elbow bursitis (inflammation of a bursa around the joint); septic arthritis not suspected at this time.

Management Plan:
- Medication: Ibuprofen 400 mg by mouth twice daily after meals; discontinue if heartburn occurs.
- Investigations: Order blood tests to screen for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout; blood test forms to be mailed to patient with instructions.
- Follow-up: Arrange follow-up appointment (in person or via phone/video) to review blood test results and assess the elbow.
- Safety: If elbow becomes very red, very painful, or the redness/spread worsens, seek urgent assessment (emergency evaluation).
- Reassurance: Current presentation not considered dangerous or life-threatening.

Patient Summary:
- A 53-year-old man presents with a week-long, non-painful left elbow swelling that is mildly warm. Exam favors bursitis rather than septic arthritis. Initiated NSAID therapy and ordered blood tests to evaluate for inflammatory/infectious/rheumatologic causes, with a follow-up visit planned after results.

Key Takeaways:
- Take Ibuprofen 400 mg by mouth twice daily after meals; stop if heartburn occurs.
- Blood tests will be mailed to you; complete them as instructed and follow up with the clinic after results.
- Seek urgent care if the elbow becomes very red, extremely painful, or the swelling rapidly worsens.

Next Steps:
- Complete and return blood tests (inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, gout screen).
- Attend or schedule follow-up (phone/video or in-person) once results are available (about 5–6 days after testing).

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs (no vitals available), medication reconciliation (no regular meds reported but not detailed beyond “none”), imaging results (none obtained), and complete allergy/drug reaction history beyond peanut allergy.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some conversational filler and phrasing, but sufficient to determine clinical plan.
